meaning.evidence: Every fact is kept: the council, the 50th anniversary, "May 1, 1976", "more than 20,000 Kurds", the Peshmerga cooperation, Mike Cortese of District 4, "signed on October 6, 2026". Additions are colour ("working shoulder to shoulder with U.S. troops").

sense.evidence: "first mob", "got hold of", "a proper hub", "gives a nod" fit. "while pulling their weight in Nashville's growth" understates "playing an important role" (doing a fair share, not an important part).

authenticity.evidence: Mostly natural ("has gone and officially marked", "The proclamation gives a big rap to the Kurdish community"), but "giving them their dues" misforms the idiom (giving them their due).

register.evidence: Plenty of Aussie phrasing but standard spelling and the original's sentence order throughout; no asides. A level-4 weight rather than a level-5 yarn.

tone.evidence: Keeps the respectful news tone under the slang: "The city's become a proper hub for Kurdish cultural and community life."

flow.evidence: Reads cleanly: "Plenty of them later settled in Nashville, Tennessee, while others set up communities in cities and states right across the country."

variety.evidence: Varied choices ("first mob", "first lot", "big rap", "gives a nod", "teaming up") with nothing leaned on.

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the VOA brief, paragraph for paragraph.

problems.why: The idiom is "give them their due"; "dues" is a misform.

problems.quote: while pulling their weight in Nashville's growth and development
problems.original: while playing an important role in Nashville's growth and development
problems.why: Pulling one's weight means doing a fair share, which understates an important role.

A.summary: Natural and faithful, a tidy level-4 news retelling with one misformed idiom.

meaning.evidence: All facts survive, but some lines shift or add: "The rest scattered and set up their own communities" turns "others" into everyone else; "And they've not just ticked a box, either." and "Not bad for a town most of us only know for country music, ay?" add claims of the narrator's own; "fifty years, the 50th anniversary" doubles up.

sense.evidence: "The Big Smoke's turned into a proper hub" strains (the Big Smoke is the big city seen from the bush, not a name for Nashville); "Here's the kicker" frames a plain statistic as a twist; "pullin' their weight in Nashville growin' up and gettin' on" garbles growth and development.

authenticity.evidence: Much reads like a real yarn ("VOA's got its mitts on the official proclamation", "workin' hand in glove with the other councillors"), but some lines feel forced: "stepped off into the U.S.", "Mates in a scrap, that lot."

register.evidence: A full level-5 retelling, with asides and direct address ("Story goes,", "So who got the ball rollin'?") and swearing within the dial ("a bloody good pat on the back").

tone.evidence: Tips from report into cheering: "Good on 'em.", "Mates in a scrap, that lot." makes the counterterrorism line breezy.

flow.evidence: Clunky joins: "fifty years, the 50th anniversary, since the first mob of Kurdish families stepped off into the U.S.", "in Nashville growin' up and gettin' on".

variety.evidence: Wide range of idiom and openers: "Story goes,", "Here's the kicker.", "the whole works", "signed, sealed and done".

essence.evidence: Still the proclamation story, but the asides ("Not bad for a town most of us only know for country music, ay?") shift it from a report on the community toward a narrator's chat.

problems.original: while playing an important role in Nashville's growth and development
problems.why: Garbled; reads as if Nashville is a person growing up, and understates the role.

B.summary: The only full level-5 yarn, lively and varied, but with garbled and strained lines and asides that tilt the news toward chat.

meaning.evidence: Essentially the original: "has officially recognised the 50th anniversary", "more than 20,000 Kurds", "signed on October 6, 2026". Nothing lost.

sense.evidence: Only a few swaps, two of which strain: "the first group of Kurdish families fronted up in the United States" (front up is to present oneself, oddly casual for immigrants arriving) and "The Big Smoke has become an important centre".

authenticity.evidence: Australian spelling ("recognised", "honouring", "councillors") is natural, but the lone "Accordin' to the document" and "The Big Smoke" are bolted onto formal prose.

register.evidence: Largely untranslated: "The proclamation highlights the Kurdish community's efforts to preserve its language, culture, and traditions over the past five decades" is the original word for word. Far off a level-5 brief.

tone.evidence: The neutral news tone is wholly intact.

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly as plain news, apart from the stray "Accordin'" against "According" two paragraphs earlier.

variety.evidence: Too little slang to vary: "fronted up", "Accordin'", "The Big Smoke".

problems.quote: The proclamation highlights the Kurdish community's efforts to preserve its language, culture, and traditions over the past five decades
problems.original: The proclamation highlights the Kurdish community's efforts to preserve its language, culture, and traditions over the past five decades
problems.why: Left untranslated, as most of the text is, against a level-5 brief.

problems.quote: fronted up in the United States
problems.why: "front up" is to present oneself or turn up somewhere expected; odd for immigrant families arriving.

problems.quote: The Big Smoke has become an important centre
problems.original: The city has become an important center
problems.why: Strained for Nashville and bolted onto formal prose.

C.summary: Little more than the original with Australian spelling and three swaps; faithful, far short of the brief.

meaning.evidence: All facts kept: "May 1, 1976", "more than 20,000 Kurds these days", the Peshmerga cooperation, "The bloke behind it was Metropolitan Nashville Council member Mike Cortese, who represents District 4", the signing date.

sense.evidence: "got its mitts on", "chipped in", "lingo", "hand in glove" fit. "The Big Smoke's turned into a real hub" strains, and "pullin' its weight" understates an important role.

authenticity.evidence: Natural voice: "So get this.", "has gone and officially marked", "it's given 'em a proper pat on the back". "the document reckons" is a touch forced for a proclamation.

register.evidence: Full drawl and slang throughout with a narrator's framing ("So get this.", "Now,"), but no real asides; just under a full level-5 yarn. No swearing, which the dial allows.

tone.evidence: Friendly but respectful; the news content keeps its weight: "singles out how Kurdish Peshmerga forces, U.S. troops and their allies have pitched in together in the fight against terrorism."

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly aloud: "Heaps of 'em ended up puttin' down roots in Nashville, Tennessee, while the rest set up communities".

variety.evidence: Good range, with "mob" repeated ("the first mob of Kurdish families", "that first mob of Kurdish families").

essence.evidence: Clearly the VOA brief, every paragraph present, retold.

D.summary: The best balance: a natural, fluent Aussie retelling that keeps every fact and the respectful tone.

meaning.evidence: All facts kept, in the original's order: "landed in the United States on May 1, 1976", "more than 20,000 Kurds", Cortese and District 4, the date.

sense.evidence: "got its mitts on", "put down roots", "chipped in" fit; "The Big Smoke's become a big hub" strains and "pullin' its weight" understates.

authenticity.evidence: Natural for the most part ("givin' 'em a pat on the back for all they've chipped in"), no stock lines bolted on.

register.evidence: Drawl and slang throughout but sentence by sentence with the original and no narrator; a level-4 weight.

tone.evidence: News tone kept: "The proclamation also gives a nod to the long-runnin' relationship between the United States and Kurdistan".

flow.evidence: Readable, but "The Big Smoke's become a big hub" right after "the biggest Kurdish communities" clunks.

variety.evidence: Repeats "first mob" (twice), "Accordin'" (twice) and "big"/"biggest" in two lines.

problems.why: Strained term for Nashville, and "big" echoes "biggest" the line before.

problems.why: "first mob" repeats from the opening sentence.

E.summary: Faithful and natural, a level-4 retelling with some repetition.
